newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp questions Loewen deal.
newsitem.headline: Service Corp questions Loewen deal.

text.p: Service Corp International said on Friday that because of Loewen Group Inc's failure to disclose fully the terms involving two acquisitions, shareholders "are unable to assess the attractiveness of these commitments."
Service Corp, which has mounted a $2.9 billion hostile bid for Loewen, raised the issue in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The filing concerns offers to exchange Loewen common and preferred stock for common stock of New Service Corp International, a holding company formed in connection with Service Corp's bid.
In Loewen's deal to acquire Prime Succession Inc, Service Corp said a third party investor is allowed to require Loewen to buy that investor's stake in Prime Succession.
At the same time, the deal would permit Loewen to require the investor to sell its interest in Prime Succession to Loewen, at undisclosed prices.
Such put and call rights are also included in the agreement to acquire the Rose Hills Co, Service Corp said, quoting press reports.

Because of Loewen's failure to disclose the put and call prices in the two transactions, "SCI believes that shareholders are unable to assess the attractiveness of these commitments," Service Corp said.
Service Corp said the acquisition of Prime Succession has been completed, while the deal involving Rose Hills is pending.
In the filing, Service Corp also noted uncertainties over the future tax rates that could apply to Loewen.

Service Corp said a proposed withholding tax regulation of the Internal Revenue Service that will become effective on January 1, 1998, may, if adopted, eliminate Loewen's current tax savings, "which could have a material impact on the company's earnings," Service Corp said.
